shows.title: Chloë Bass: Soft Services
shows.description:
A Henry OffSite commission of fourteen engraved stone benches placed singly and in small groups around Volunteer Park on Capitol Hill, plus two more sculptures outside the Henry on the UW campus. Each stone carries a short text by the New York artist Chloë Bass, set in Optima, the typeface of Maya Lin's Vietnam Veterans Memorial, and the silhouette of a plant (black locust, alder or western juniper) printed in light-responsive pigment that shifts with the weather and time of day.

The title comes from the 'soft services' that AIDS activists were able to fund in the crisis years, care such as massage or meal trains that insurance did not cover, and the project links that history of Volunteer Park to questions of care, memorial and who gets support. It was organized by Shamim M. Momin and is free to visit in the park.

shows.description:
RIPE is a solo show of new work by Zoe Potter about aging, time and the way beauty is looked at and used up, written from a woman's point of view. The idea of ripeness, something at its peak and about to be consumed or thrown away, runs through the show.

The works are in glass, bronze, steel and latex: pulled and slumped glass, small bronze flies and ants on the walls, latex that slowly breaks down, and a steel spider-like figure hanging from the ceiling. The museum has not posted images of the works yet; shown here are recent works by the artist, including a black glass and steel figure from her September 2026 showing at SOIL and recent paintings.

shows.title: Northwest Trolls: Way of the Bird King
shows.description:
Frankie Feetsplinters, a giant troll built from salvaged wood by the Danish recycling artist Thomas Dambo, stands outside the National Nordic Museum's entrance in Ballard. Clad in shingle-like scraps, the grinning figure is the only city dweller among six trolls Dambo placed around the region in 2023 (on Bainbridge Island and Vashon Island, in Issaquah and West Seattle, and in Portland) for Northwest Trolls: Way of the Bird King.

The trolls are characters in an environmental story Dambo wrote, and the project is meant to send people out exploring and to show that trash can become something beautiful. Frankie was built with volunteers and unveiled on September 18, 2023; the series was presented by the Scan Design Foundation with the Paul G. Allen Family Foundation. Dambo gives a talk at the museum on October 20, 2026.

shows.title: A Ballard Story: Pacific Fishermen
shows.description:
A history exhibition about Seattle's working waterfront, told through Pacific Fishermen, Inc., one of the last working shipyards in Ballard, whose site on Salmon Bay has served shipbuilders and fishing families for more than 150 years. It follows the landscape before and after settlement, shipbuilding and commercial fishing on the bay, immigrant and multigenerational fishing families, the dangers of the work, and local historian Doug Dixon's efforts to preserve Ballard's history.

The show uses historic photographs, artifacts, interactive displays and excerpts from 16 oral history interviews recorded between 2000 and 2026 for the museum's Nordic American Voices and Vanishing Generations projects. The images are a launch photograph from MOHAI's Seattle Post-Intelligencer collection and a crab-boat photograph lent by Herbjorg Pedersen.

shows.title: The Story of the Salute
shows.description:
A history exhibition about the raised-fist protest on the medal podium of the 200 meters at the 1968 Mexico City Olympics, when Americans Tommie Smith and John Carlos, backed by Australian silver medalist Peter Norman, used the ceremony to protest racism and inequality. It also covers sociologist Harry Edwards and the Olympic Project for Human Rights, which inspired the gesture, and what the three athletes faced afterward.

The museum opened it in June 2026, timed to the FIFA World Cup match between the USA and Australia in Seattle on Juneteenth. The pictures are the archival photographs of the podium and of the four men that the museum uses for the exhibit.

shows.title: Chronicles of a Global East
shows.description:
A third-floor collection gallery about the premodern world linked by the Silk Roads and the sea routes of maritime Asia, where artistic traditions crossed borders. Its centerpiece is a large 18th-century Chinese wall hanging painted on pieced deerskin that maps Tainan, the Taiwanese port with Dutch-built forts and Chinese and Indigenous residents.

Also on view are an imperial Chinese mirror showing Chinese palaces in a European-style pastoral landscape, a reversal of chinoiserie, and Vietnamese blue-and-white export ceramics that imitate Chinese porcelain and were lost in a shipwreck on their way to market. The gallery frames each borrowing as both a claim of advantage and an act of curiosity. The images show the deerskin map (detail and full) and Vietnamese blue-and-white wares from SAM's collection.

shows.title: Cosmic Beings in Mesoamerican and Andean Art
shows.description:
SAM's third-floor gallery of ancient art from Mesoamerica and the Andes. Ceramic vessels, stone sculpture, textiles and ornaments show ancestors, gods, humans, supernatural animals and monsters, reflecting belief systems about the origin of the universe and the relationship between the human and cosmic worlds, from shamanic transformation to animal spirit companions.

The gallery opens with a pair of Maya limestone door-reveal panels from Campeche, Mexico (ca. AD 550-950). The other images are highlights of SAM's ancient American collection: an Aztec priest of the rain god Tlaloc, a Maya cylinder vase with scribes in the underworld, a Wari four-cornered hat, Moche stirrup-spout vessels and a Maya standing priest.

shows.title: Art and Life Along the Northwest Coast
shows.description:
SAM's third-floor gallery of Native art from the Pacific Northwest, showing how First Peoples shaped their lives, oral traditions and ceremonies around the water, forests, valleys and mountains of the region. Baskets, carved and painted wood, masks, hats and regalia from Coast Salish, Tlingit, Kwakwaka'wakw, Haida and other nations are on view.

The museum's page features a coiled cedar-root basket (1900-30) by Sauk weaver Susan Wawatkin Bedal. The other images are highlights of SAM's Northwest Coast collection: the Tlingit Raven Screen (ca. 1810), an interior housepost by Arthur Shaughnessy, a Willie Seaweed Crooked Beak mask, a Makah lidded basket, a Tlingit Sea Bear crest hat and a bent-corner chest.
shows.dates_note: Ongoing collection installation; SAM lists no opening or closing date

shows.title: A Noble Tension
shows.description:
A fourth-floor gallery of African figurative sculpture. Men and women carved for altars and shrines fill the cases; many were made to call on deities for help with life on earth, and their taut, composed stances express that duty. Some were consulted in quiet shrines, others carried into festivals with music, dance and song.

At the center of the room is a Ghanaian figurative coffin in the shape of a Mercedes-Benz by Kane Quaye (1991), and one wall case is devoted to Yoruba art from Nigeria. The images show works from SAM's African collection, including a Kongo nkisi figure, a Yoruba Ile Ori and Epa mask, and royal and standing figures; the last image is a view of the gallery with the coffin.
shows.dates_note: Ongoing collection installation; SAM lists no opening or closing date

shows.title: Conscious Constructions
shows.description:
A fourth-floor gallery of European painting and sculpture spanning the High Renaissance, Mannerism and the Baroque, with a few contemporary works mixed in. The selection is about deliberate composition: figures who meet our gaze, objects placed to lead the eye into the picture, and still lifes of luxury goods that remind viewers of the passing of time.

The gallery opens with Balthasar van der Ast's Still Life with Cherries (1617), a recent gift. The other images are 17th-century highlights of SAM's European collection: Johan de Cordua's vanitas still life, Rubens's The Last Supper, Michaelina Wautier's Boys Blowing Bubbles, Georges de La Tour's Saint Sebastian Tended by Saint Irene, Zurbarán's The Flight into Egypt and Abraham Janssens's The Origin of the Cornucopia.
shows.dates_note: Ongoing collection installation; SAM lists no opening or closing date

shows.title: Now and Forever
shows.description:
A gallery of 16th-century Italian portraits, painted when prosperous citizens began commissioning likenesses once reserved for royalty. Costume, gesture and accessories signal family and social role, while faces and gazes hint at personality; some portraits marked a new job or a marriage, or kept the image of a son far from home.

The works hang with objects of the kind that filled the same wealthy homes, next to SAM's wood-paneled Italian Room. The museum features Santi di Tito's Portrait of a Young Woman (1565); the other images are Italian Renaissance portraits from SAM's Kress collection by Tintoretto, Francesco Traballesi, Girolamo da Carpi and Bernardino de' Conti, and Giambologna's marble Cupid.
shows.dates_note: Ongoing collection installation; SAM lists no opening or closing date

shows.title: Only Connect: The Art of Devotion
shows.description:
A fourth-floor gallery of Christian art from Italy and northern Europe, mostly from the 14th and 15th centuries, when churches and monasteries were the main patrons. Gold leaf and costly mineral pigments gave the early altarpieces their rich surfaces; later, oil paint made holy figures look more natural and approachable.

Many panels are fragments of larger altarpieces broken up and sold in the 19th century. The museum features Gherardo di Giovanni del Fora's Adoration of the Christ Child (ca. 1475); the other images are early Italian panels from SAM's Kress collection by Pietro Lorenzetti, Bernardo Daddi, the Master of San Torpè, Lorenzo Monaco, the Master of the Straus Madonna and Giovanni di Paolo.
shows.dates_note: Ongoing collection installation; SAM lists no opening or closing date

shows.title: Porcelain Room
shows.description:
SAM's Porcelain Room on the fourth floor revives the European fashion, in the 17th and 18th centuries, for rooms lined floor to ceiling with porcelain from China, Japan and the new European factories. More than a thousand European and Asian pieces from the collection are grouped by color and theme rather than by country or maker, under a ceiling fresco by Giovanni Battista Tiepolo, and digital kiosks let visitors zoom in on each object.

The images show 18th-century French porcelain from the Vincennes and Sèvres factories, gifts of Ulrich and Stella Fritzsche that are on view in the room: a snake-handled bowl, Bouillard cups, breakfast and tea services, a flower vase, a three-legged teapot, wine coolers and a pomade pot. The last image is a view of the room. Diego Cibelli's porcelain installation is also on view here (separate card).
shows.dates_note: Ongoing collection installation; SAM lists no opening or closing date

shows.title: Ann Leda Shapiro: Inner Cosmologies
shows.description:
A survey of the Vashon Island painter Ann Leda Shapiro (born 1946), winner of SAM's 2025 Betty Bowen Award, bringing together watercolors from across fifty years, some never exhibited. Her early work, made between New York and the Bay Area in the 1970s, is exuberantly feminist and gender-fluid, asking what is male and what is female.

In the 1980s, volunteering at an acupuncture clinic for people with AIDS in Texas led her to study and practice Chinese medicine, and her paintings since have pictured the body as an environment of energy flows linked to nature and the cosmos. The first three images are Shapiro works in SAM's collection (Woman Landing on Man in the Moon and Two Sides, both 1971, and Alone with My Feelings, 1974); the museum has not posted a checklist, so the others are works by the artist from François Ghebaly Gallery.

shows.title: Art Without Walls
shows.description:
The permanent collection of the Olympic Sculpture Park: twenty-two large works across nine acres on Seattle's waterfront, always on view and free. They include Alexander Calder's The Eagle, Richard Serra's Wake, Louise Bourgeois's Eye Benches and Father and Son, Mark di Suvero's Schubert Sonata, Teresita Fernández's Seattle Cloud Cover, Roxy Paine's Split, Tony Smith's Stinger, Beverly Pepper's Perre's Ventaglio III and Mark Dion's Neukom Vivarium.

The newest addition is Jaume Plensa's Echo, a tall white head facing Mount Olympus across the bay. The park's Z-shaped design connects four Northwest landscapes (meadow, aspen grove, evergreen valley and shoreline), each a setting for the art. The last image is an aerial view of the park.
